previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including end-stage renal disease, a functioning transplanted pancreas, mechanical mitral valve, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted for planned revascularization due to a non-healing left foot ulcer. During admission, she developed healthcare-associated pneumonia with fever, cough, and hypoxia, leading to transfer to the medicine service. She was treated with intravenous vancomycin, levaquin, and flagyl, with improvement in symptoms and radiographic findings. Her INR was subtherapeutic at discharge, requiring continuation of heparin infusion at a rehabilitation facility until therapeutic range was achieved. The revascularization procedure was postponed due to active infection. She completed a 10-day antibiotic course for both pneumonia and foot infection, with stable graft function and wound care arranged for follow-up. She was discharged to extended care with plans for vascular surgery follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to the Vascular Surgery Service for 
evaluation and treatment on ___.

Neuro: The patient received oral pain medications.

CV: The patient remained stable from a cardiovascular 
standpoint; vital signs were routinely monitored. Patient was 
taken to angio ___ and a stent was placed in the left 
popliteal artery. See operative note for further details. 
Following the procedure, the patient was recovered on the floor 
per routine post angiogram protocol. The left foot was routinely 
checked and had dopplerable pulses in the left foot. It was warm 
on discharge. the patient will be seen in 4 weeks for 
evaluation. The patient should continue on aspirin and coumadin 
for ___ to assist in stent patentcy. 

Pulmonary: The patient remained stable from a pulmonary 
standpoint; vital signs were routinely monitored. cough 
suppressants were stopped as the patient's cough had largely 
resolved. Albuterol and ipratropium nebulizer treatment were 
given. CXR done preop demonstrated improvement in infiltrate. 
See attached report.

GI/GU/FEN: Post-operatively, the patient was made NPO with IV 
fluids. Diet was advanced when appropriate, which was well 
tolerated.  Patient's intake and output were closely monitored.  
Electrolytes were routinely followed. Hemodialysis was performed 
___. Next session will be ___. Loperamide was not given 
as the patient did not have significant diarrhea during this 
admission. can consider restarting if diarrhea resumes.

closely watched for signs of infection.  No antibiotics were 
administered.

Hematology: The patient's complete blood count was examined 
routinely; no packed red cell transfusions were required. IV 
heparin was continued at a rate of 800 units per hour from 
arrival until the patient was taken to the angiography suite. 
Coumadin was held preprocedure. INR preprocedure remained 
elevated so 2 units of fresh frozen plasma were administered. 
The patient was restarted on coumadin the night of ___ and 
IV heparin at 800 units per hour was adminsitered beginning at 
1159 ___ on ___. The patient had a therapeutic PTT at the 
time of discharge on this same dose. Plan is for continued IV 
heparin bridge at rehab until INR ___. Indication is 
mechanical valve. Aspirin was continued.

At the time of discharge, the patient was doing well, afebrile 
with stable vital signs.  The patient was tolerating a regular 
diet and pain was well controlled.  The patient received 
discharge teaching and follow-up instructions with understanding 
verbalized and agreement with the discharge plan.

Division of Vascular and Endovascular Surgery
Lower Extremity Angioplasty/Stent Discharge Instructions
 

MEDICATION:

·     Take Aspirin and coumadin daily 

·     Continue all other medications you were taking before 
surgery, unless otherwise directed

·     You make take Tylenol or prescribed pain medications for 
any post procedure pain or discomfort

 

WHAT TO EXPECT:

It is normal to have slight swelling of the legs:

·     Elevate your leg above the level of your heart with 
pillows every ___ hours throughout the day and night

·     Avoid prolonged periods of standing or sitting without 
your legs elevated

·     It is normal to feel tired and have a decreased appetite, 
your appetite will return with time 

·     Drink plenty of fluids and eat small frequent meals

·     It is important to eat nutritious food options (high 
fiber, lean meats, vegetables/fruits, low fat, low cholesterol) 
to maintain your strength and assist in wound healing

·     To avoid constipation: eat a high fiber diet and use stool 
softener while taking pain medication

 

ACTIVITIES:

·     When you go home, you ___ walk and use stairs

·     You ___ shower (let the soapy water run over groin 
incision, rinse and pat dry)

·     Your incision ___ be left uncovered, unless you have small 
amounts of drainage from the wound, then place a dry dressing or 
band aid over the area 

·     No heavy lifting, pushing or pulling (greater than 5 lbs) 
for 1 week (to allow groin puncture to heal)

·     After 1 week, you ___ resume sexual activity

·     After 1 week, gradually increase your activities and 
distance walked as you can tolerate

·     No driving until you are no longer taking pain medications

 

CALL THE OFFICE FOR: ___
·     Numbness, coldness or pain in lower extremities 

·     Temperature greater than 101.5F for 24 hours

·     New or increased drainage from incision or white, yellow 
or green drainage from incisions

·     Bleeding from groin puncture site

 

SUDDEN, SEVERE BLEEDING OR SWELLING (Groin puncture site)

·     Lie down, keep leg straight and have someone apply firm 
pressure to area for 10 minutes. If bleeding stops, call 
vascular office ___. If bleeding does not stop, call 
___ for transfer to closest Emergency Room.
